name: jones_single_ccz_measured_four_t_lowering
precondition: dv_recon / Toffoli-level IRCircuit; needs toffoli (at least one ccz or ccx present), needs ancilla_room, measurement and classically controlled gates allowed; qubits <= 24. No rotations, no shared control pairs and no span condition required - every single ccz/ccx qualifies on its own.
identity: Lower EACH individual CCZ/CCX in isolation, not pairs. For a gate CCZ(x,y,z) (for CCX(x,y;z) the same with cz(a,z) replaced by cx(a,z)): take one fresh clean ancilla a in |0>, emit and_compute(x, y -> a) [Gidney's temporary-AND: 4 T, T-depth 1], then cz(a, z), then and_uncompute(a) [0 T: H on a, measure a, and on outcome 1 apply the classically controlled cz(x, y) fix-up, returning a to |0>]. Total 4 T per gate instead of the 7 T of the unitary Toffoli decomposition. The compute/uncompute brackets the gate immediately, so the ancilla's lifetime is three ops long: it is closed before the next match opens, ONE ancilla is reused by all 11 gates (qubits 14 -> 15), nothing about the surrounding op list is assumed, and no commutation analysis is needed. Matches are emitted one per ccz/ccx occurrence, in circuit order.
correctness: CCZ(x,y,z) is diagonal with eigenvalue (-1)^{xyz}; it therefore depends on x,y only through the Boolean product xy. If a carries xy then CZ(a,z) has eigenvalue (-1)^{(xy)z} = (-1)^{xyz} on every computational basis state, hence the two operators agree as operators and so on arbitrary superpositions (same for CCX, a permutation depending on x,y only through xy). Gidney's temporary-AND gadget (arXiv:1709.06648 Fig. 3, after Jones arXiv:1212.5069) prepares a = x AND y on a clean |0> ancilla using 4 T gates, exactly and unitarily. Its uncompute measures a in the X basis: the measurement collapses a but leaves a residual phase kickback (-1)^{m·xy} with m the outcome, which is removed exactly by the classically controlled CZ(x,y); after the fix-up the state is the original one on x,y,z with a back in |0>, for every branch and with the SAME branch coefficient for every input, so the branch-wise specification check (invariant 2: ancillas |0> -> |0>, phase consistency c_m independent of x) passes with Sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1. Error is exactly zero, so no budget is drawn. Jones' count is optimal-known for a single Toffoli with one ancilla and measurement: 4 T, versus 7 T for any unitary ancilla-free decomposition, which is why a purely unitary optimizer (pyzx at 47) cannot reach it.
trigger: Scan the op list once for gates with name in {ccz, ccx}. Emit one match per occurrence, carrying its position and its three wires, with the AND pair chosen as the two controls for ccx and, for ccz, as the two wires whose removal leaves the wire that is read least often nearby (any choice is correct; fix it deterministically as the two smallest wire indices for reproducibility). The only guards are: a clean ancilla is obtainable (append_ancillas / reuse of a closed one) and the gate has three distinct wires. There is no condition on neighbouring ops, so the trigger matches all 11 ccz of adder_6.
expected_effect: All 11 ccz of adder_6 drop from 7 T to 4 T each: 11*7 = 77 -> 11*4 = 44 T, i.e. -33 T (-42.9%), crossing the best baseline pyzx at 47 by 3 T. CNOT count rises by about 2 per gate and the qubit count by exactly 1 (14 -> 15) because the single ancilla is closed and reused after each gate; cost order is lexicographic in (T, qubits, CNOT), so the T drop decides. This is strictly per-gate and therefore immune to the failure mode of the span-sharing idea in history.json: no shared control pair, no 'controls unwritten over the span' hypothesis, nothing to invalidate. If some ccz are later also pair-shareable, that is an independent further win on top, but it is not assumed here.
source: Cody Jones, 'Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate', Phys. Rev. A 87, 022328 (2013), arXiv:1212.5069 (Toffoli with 4 T using one ancilla and measurement with classically controlled fix-up); Craig Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018), arXiv:1709.06648 (the temporary-AND compute/uncompute gadget form used here)
